lines.text: It's DVDASA. Sometimes I like to say it, Davidiza. [beat] That was good, whatever that was. Oh yeah.
[announcer voice] You are now entering... entering... an alternate universe... [echo] universe, universe, universe, universe...
[music] Walk them one, walk them all -- it's DVDASA! Here we go. We've got special guest Sam, we've got special guest Fredo. Hey. Hello. We've got little money, we've got big money. We got Asa.

We got Valentin. And the hostess with the mostest, Dicho. [warmly] Oh, thanks, Bobby. Take it away. You're too kind, you're too kind. Welcome to the show -- it's DVDASA. Like the man said, we've got big money and little money here today.
And that music right now is just a little impromptu jam session by Maximum Hedrum. And I'll get to how this unholy union all came to be -- how this shit went fucking down.

For those of you who listen to the show, you know a few weeks ago me and Harry took off to film the fourth installment of our travel show, Thumbs Up. And what can I say -- I'm addicted to the road. I don't know what to say about that. It's like I've been traveling non-stop...

...on the road since I can remember, even little road trips my parents would take. And for someone like me who doesn't do drugs, that's escape, that's fantasy. What happens on the road is real, but it sort of isn't. You get in a car, you get on a plane, and all of a sudden you're away from your home, your...

...schedule, your environment, your friends, your family. And just like that you can be in another country where they don't speak the language, all kinds of shit, and you're far away from home, running away from your problems -- or at least I am. Detached. So what problems were you running away from on this trip?

I was actually getting really... I get into this super Howard Hughes kind of thing -- don't leave the house, piss in jars, fuck everyone. And you know, I do this podcast, but it's just me and these guys in this room.

Work, and coming here -- I started really hating people, hating humanity. And then I think, fuck, if I get back on the road I'm going to be forced to deal with people, and I can reconnect with a human side, lean less on my serial-killer side.

So this time you were facing your problems head on. [beat] Wow, didn't even think about it like that. Look at you. But I always think of the road as, like, 'see you when I see you.' Like, hey, didn't you say you were going to take me to dinner tonight? Or, hey, that thing you owe me? And I'm like...
...yeah, gotta hit the road, I'll see you when I get back. Whatever shit you needed from me -- now you can't get it. I'm gone. So that was the answer.
And one of the things that's glaring, where the road is actually not fantasy, it's reality, is when you get arrested. When you're like, hey, I'm in fucking Bolivia, I'm in China...

...they don't speak English, so I must be able to do whatever I want. And that's a very ignorant American stance, which I've been a part of. When I travel around the world and I act a fool, most times I get away with it.

When I don't get away with it is when reality blasts me in the face with prison time or whatever. And so -- not allowed into Japan, not allowed into Canada. We came to a point on this trip where we were in Detroit, which is one of the worst, most decrepit cities. I love Detroit, but the actual economic reality of that city...

...is that it's a ghost town, it's completely fucked up. And we were trying to go all the way across the country. From Detroit you have a choice: go through the rest of, like, Cleveland -- I forget our route -- we could have gone south...

...east, or we could have gone up through Windsor into Canada, which I'm not allowed into. The last time I attempted was Thumbs Up season two, four or five years ago, and they said, 'yeah, you're tripping.' It's a little weird to be told, hey, you're not allowed into Canada, because it's not like there's a wall or anything. It's like, hey, you can't come.

It's like someone saying, hey, you can't come across the street -- there's an imaginary wall. It's not Tijuana, which is super hard to cross, with barbed wire and huge walls. It's literally, you walk across the street and you're in Canada. So the first time, I avoided all of Canada by just flying over and going straight to Alaska.

But this time we got to the border. We hitched a ride, we got to the border, and our camera crew met up with us. So basically it's me, Harry, and a cameraman hitchhiking, and there's a van following us with extra batteries, water...

...and weapons and shit, just in case we get in trouble. At this point we've been on the road for two weeks, we look and smell like shit, and we get to the Canadian border. And we had like a thousand dollars' worth of fireworks, medieval weaponry, knives, ninja stars, swords.

What are the ninja stars for? [laughing] Look, if you're a kid growing up in America, you're fascinated by ninjas. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, ninjas from the '80s. Especially if you're a kid in the '80s, right?

If you're a kid in the '80s -- ninjas rode skateboards, they ate pizza. And the ninja stars, they're just sick, they look awesome. But most of the time when you bought them online or mail-order, they weren't sharp.

They made them blunt on the end, or they were plastic. I bought a lot of ninja stars when I went to China, and I got some at a hardware store in Oregon once, and I just started carrying them everywhere I went. I got really fucking good with them. You know, in the movies they're like--

[mimes throwing] --and they hit everything. When you're a kid you're just throwing it at the wall hoping it'll stick. It's like all those throwing sports -- it's follow-through, wherever your finger ends up pointing. So I'd be in hotel rooms just throwing the ninja star at the wall over and over again.

I got pretty good at it. So on this trip? Yeah -- well, over the last couple years. I might be a little rusty now. But you really think you're going to get into a fight on the road and go, 'hold on a second,' run to the van, grab your ninja stars, and throw them?
Don't need to go to the van -- the ninja stars are on me. Oh, okay. At all times. And number two: there are a lot of things in life where, like, if you pull out a gun, someone sees the gun--
Oh, so it's just the threat of a ninja star. If you're in Detroit and you see an Asian guy -- I look somewhat normal now, but I had a white suit on and blonde hair...

...there aren't that many Asians in Detroit. If you're walking down the street thinking 'let's mug this motherfucker,' and the guy pulls out five ninja stars -- that's not something you see every day. To pull that out in a fight, you're going to think, or I'm just assuming, 'wow, this guy probably knows how...

...to use that, and I'd like to keep my eyes intact.' But they probably have guns. They probably do have guns. What are you going to do with ninja stars in a gunfight? I'd aim for the face, anywhere in the face. Well, if you're a ninja, they're not even going to see you coming.

Yeah, they're going to be dead before they even know you're there. [deadpan] So far the only two things the ninja star has been used for on the trip is to scale a fish and to open a cardboard box with tape on it.

So for some reason they skipped all of that. They didn't see our fucking bolt cutters, they didn't see any of our weapons -- they just saw the box of fireworks. So they go, 'you guys pull over here to customs.' And I'm already saying, let's just go through Michigan or whatever, we're not going to get in.

The lady even goes, 'has any of you ever had trouble getting into the country?' And I'm like, yes, I have. And they go, 'okay, explain what happened.' Basically, in the States, if you have a criminal record as a kid, when you turn 18 they get rid of it. In Canada they keep it open for like 10, 20 more...

...years. So I'm like, shit, I'm 37 right now, hopefully they closed it by now. So we go sit in the waiting room of the Canadian customs border from Windsor to Detroit. Our van is a giant white Sprinter van, and a giant black Sprinter van pulls up right next to it -- and then a freak show comes out.

A giant black guy comes out, this guy with a huge afro comes out. I was with Critter, and he's like, 'oh, these are our evil doppelgangers.' And I was like, well, what if we're the evil doppelgangers and they're the good guys?

There were six of you guys. Six of us -- so there are six of these guys, and they come out, they got checked at customs too. Oh, this was you guys? Yeah. Oh, this is the story of how you guys met! I didn't even know.
Okay, I'm getting to it, I'm getting to it. So they come in, and I had barely met Fredo for two seconds through Money Mark at a Yeah Yeah Yeahs concert a few months ago.
Oh, yeah, I'm with that. So Fredo's like, 'hey, what's up, man, I met you with Mark.' And I was like, oh yeah, yeah. And I'm like, oh, we're in this band, Maximum Hedrum.

And turns out -- I don't know how the fuck this happened -- they kept us there for an hour, but then they're like, 'yeah, you guys can go in.' And we're like, oh, cool. And then you guys had, like, a fucking DUI bass player. We had everybody in our crew--

We found out who was a thug. Yeah, that's a real quick way to find out, because Canadians are thorough. You think you know everything about Mark and Asa and Bobby, and then you go to Canada and find out who's a pedophile, who killed someone. So they find out their bass player has, like...

...two DUIs, all this shit back in the day. Fredo and I got busted. Well -- we actually got away with it. Doing what? We were driving, leaving Canada, going home, having the best time ever. Someone had given us a joint...

...and they were smoking it. I didn't realize the border was coming up in a few minutes. I was like, oh shit, we're really high now. Oh shit, there's the border. This would only happen to a fucking pothead.
So we shove it under the seat and I go, 'oh no, this is it, we're busted.' And he's like, 'you haven't smoked anything in months, you haven't touched it.' And I was like, what? Okay, right.
So we pull over, we go in, and they didn't even keep us that long. But they found the weed? No -- they checked the car and they didn't find it.
So they go, 'okay, you guys can go.' We get in the car. They call me back first. Then we start driving away and they call you back. The guy goes, 'hey, wait a minute, wait a minute--'
'Mr. Ortiz.' Oh, shit. Oh, fuck. He walks back and says, 'what's your ID again? Okay, thank you.' And that was it, and we drove off. Nice.
But the Canadian border is notorious as the hardest border to cross in North America, for sure. Nico, do you know that story? No. Is it weird to hear your dad talk about that stuff?

No. No? You're like, 'I don't give a fuck.' Do you smoke weed? Yeah, sometimes. Oh, okay. [warmly] Wow, what a cool father and son. Only once. Yeah, I've often wondered what I'd be like if I ever have kids. Because I'm just like, thank everybody, fuck this--
Well, at this point he's 18. Yeah, but before he was 18? Zilch, nothing. But whatever -- for the past six months he knows, he knows all the Beastie Boys songs. Looking down the mirror--

Right, pretty much. So it's completely random, we just happened to be stopped at the border at the same time. So we get out and -- I couldn't believe you sent me that thing. I was like, what is going on? Fredo took a picture of me...

...and Critter just walking with a giant box of fireworks, and we had to identify each firework and what it does, and we're like, is this necessary? From our perspective, we're walking into the border check and there are these two weirdos with bleached beards, yeah, wearing...

...like a huge American flag shirt, and we're like, who are these dudes? And the chairs are facing out, so you're watching whoever's coming in. The Canadians working there were like, what the fuck is happening right now? What the heck is going on?
So did they think you guys were together? Yeah, that's what I was thinking too, because we were talking-- Well, you're in similar vans. Very similar vans. You all look not normal.
You all look like weirdos. Yeah. So we get the okay, and I'm like, whoa, that's cool. Maybe it helped that they were there -- because two weirdos is somehow way more threatening than a group.

Yeah, I was like, let's just start figuring out what our route's going to be, because there's no fucking way we're getting in. And Critter was like, 'a hundred percent we're getting in.' And I'm like, what are you talking about?

We've already been here for an hour, they're fucking with us. He's like, 'Dave, start thinking positive.' And I'm like, all right, shit. So yeah -- I was positive they were going to say, 'okay, you guys can't come in today.'

And they were like, 'yeah, have a nice time.' And I'm like, oh, shit. So immediately, the first thing we do about 10 feet after we get in -- we break the law, we start hitchhiking in Canada, right at the border. A lot of the cars leaving...

...the border are border patrol cops, so we're like, ah, fuck. So maybe an hour later these guys leave, and we're like, let's flag down these guys. So they pick us up and give us a fucking awesome ride into Canada.
Where did we eat? Wait, what were you guys doing? Are you Canadian? No, we were doing this -- we had a show the next day in Toronto. Okay. And we'd had a show the previous day.

Where, in Chicago? Chicago, yeah. So it was totally a coincidence, it was fucking awesome. So I get picked up with Critter by these guys. I barely know Fredo, we talked a little at the border, but these guys are all cool, and they're like...

...'yeah, we're opening for the Yeah Yeah Yeahs in Toronto tomorrow.' And I'm like, fuck, that's one of my favorite bands, love them. And they say, there's a song about just hugging one another. That's right up your alley. Yeah, we're just gonna hug the shit out of--

You know, Sam was explaining it -- we have this song where we get everyone in the audience to hug each other. But there are a lot of goths that show up to the Yeah Yeah Yeahs concerts, and they're like, don't touch me. Don't touch me.

So they're like, 'hey, do you and Critter want to come and be our hug ambassadors?' And we're like, fuck, we would love that. That's like what you'd be doing anyway. Yeah. So -- okay, cool, awesome. And it was weird for me being in Canada, because I hate Canadians and I hate Canada, and...

...now I was inside, and these guys picked us up and they're all cool. Wait, wait -- you hate Canadians too? You know when you hate something and you don't know why? You're like, there's no reason for me to hate this, they didn't do anything to me--

Or you meet somebody and they're really Canadian. Canada to America is New Jersey to New York. It's weird, they didn't do shit to me. I just don't like them, they're just too nice. Too nice. Or maybe I'm projecting something onto them. Just fuck them all, fuck them all.

I don't know what it is. It's because I travel a lot, and when I travel, Americans are proud in a very arrogant, ignorant, 'we're Americans' way. And the Canadians are like, 'we have this maple leaf, this red fucking maple leaf.' Oh, Bobby was just wearing one.

Bobby loves Canada, he loves it more than anything. And they sew it onto their backpacks so no one thinks they're American. And they're like, 'we can go anywhere we want in the world, our passport gets us in anywhere, because we don't have beef with anybody.'

'We're Canadian. Peace. We're cool with everybody. We don't pick sides. No judging.' And I'm just like, I fucking hate you. I don't know why I hate you, but I fucking hate your guts. I don't know why you hate it--

There's something unrespectable about a country that's never been to war. Except that one Pussy Riot girl -- she got busted. Oh, she was Canadian? Yeah. So I'm like, hey Mark, we just ran into Fredo, and Money Mark's like, 'oh shit, dude, I know those guys.' And actually Mark wrote 'Hugs' with us. So it goes--

Oh yeah -- so Mark's like... I told him, hey, we're going to do this hug song with them tomorrow, and Mark's like, 'yeah, I wrote that song.' And I was like, dude, this is crazy, this is fucking bonkers. And then we were chilling in Canada that night, and of course I Wikipedia'd all these guys. I'm like, who the fuck just picked us...

...up right now? Find out Fredo's been the drummer for the Beastie Boys for like 15 years. Derrick, the black guy -- the only black guy that's ever picked us up hitchhiking -- is the lead singer of Sepultura, which is one of my favorite metal bands. Except I didn't know what any of them looked...

...like, so he's just, 'oh yeah,' and I'm like, what? He's just a black dude from Cleveland, Ohio who ended up being the lead singer of a metal band from Sao Paulo, and he has a crazy story. And then we've got Sam -- Sam Spiegel, a million musical projects, N.A.S.A....
...the opera with Karen O, Maximum Hedrum, all this shit. I saw your Wikipedia -- it's like, Spike Jonze's brother. Do people just throw that in all the time? You work with your brother--

You score movies, you do music. I do work with him, but for sure, growing up, that was a prerequisite. Are you older or younger? I'm 10 years younger. And is it just annoying as shit when that happens?
You know, I used to really resent it. It used to drive me crazy, because that was my introduction before my name, always. That was what defined me, and it used to bum me out.

But then it got easy after a while to recognize the people who were jocking me because of that, versus for who I was. And as I started to do my own shit, I was able to recognize, these are the people jocking me for the shit I'm doing...

...too, versus just liking me for who I am, for my personality. It taught me how to suss that stuff out. But yeah, it used to bug me. I mean, we talked about this before -- like hanging out with John Lennon's...

...son. Anytime, everyone's like, 'oh, you're the brother of,' or 'the son of.' You can't just be your own person. But after I got the ride from you guys -- I didn't know you guys pre-ride -- it's like, I know, I've listened to the Beastie Boys, I...

I love Sepultura, and that song you did with Karen O for the Adidas commercial, 'Hello Tomorrow' -- that shit was awesome. All these projects, I'm like, oh, we just got picked up by a supergroup, this is...

...awesome. So we spent all day fucking around in Toronto the next day, and then we get to see these guys, and I have no idea what they're going to sound like, because the musical backgrounds are all over the place. I'm like, is Derrick just going to come out and start growling--

So they come out in all checkered suits except for the bass player, and you guys were awesome, I loved it. I was like, oh, these guys are fucking amazing, we've got to have them on the podcast when we come back. And for the final song they did the hug song, and you guys were the ambassadors, and we were wearing...

...these beyond-cartoonish outfits of Canada-- Oh shit, look who's here, Harry Kim! Hey, Harry. Harry, chill out there for a second, we'll bring you in in a little bit. I want to spend this time with these guys -- you're not off the hook. Drink some water, drink a lot of water. So, uh...
...I'm wearing a shirt with a Canadian flag and it just says 'eh' under it, and Critter was wearing a Canadian necktie. I don't think it's 'eh,' I think it's 'eh.'

How does that end up in the vernacular? One guy said it and then it's for an entire nation forever -- 'eh.' It happened to us at lunch. Sam accidentally spilled some water on our tour manager, and the waitress goes, 'oh, it almost got you, eh?'
In my mind I'm like, she said it, it's real, it's official in Canada. Yeah. I mean, Toronto -- I hadn't been there since I was 18, and the women are so fucking beautiful.
Wait, and then what? You guys just hugged and then everyone in the crowd hugged? No -- so Sam's like, 'this is our hug song coming up right now.'

'These are our hug ambassadors.' And we stood out because -- oh my god, you guys got pointed out and then went through the whole crowd? We went through the whole crowd and hugged, like, 70 percent dudes, 30 percent -- it was awesome. Oh, so you weren't hugging each other? Oh no, we were hugging everyone in the audience. Was anyone--
Like, 'don't touch me'? Oh yeah. You hugged them anyway? Yeah. Critter is the best. You could tell, because they'll be like this -- there'll be people like, yeah, hug me...
...and we'll be like, yeah. And then there'll be a guy who walks away a little standoffish, and Critter will just come in like-- Were there girls? There were girls, but...

Did you hug the girls? That's a little inappropriate, we hugged mostly men. Why is that inappropriate? I don't know. What are you talking about? That could be considered molesting. No -- they were spreading international love.

The song is about-- Yeah, it's 'Hugs for Everybody.' Yeah, maybe in Canada. Hugs for everybody. Hugs for everybody. We didn't hug anyone who was like, 'get the fuck away from me.' Everyone was in the spirit.
There were a couple, whatever. I love this, you guys should have hug ambassadors at every show. It was awesome, a lot of people were into it. And then we stayed for the Yeah Yeah Yeahs concert.
And afterwards, we were just fucking with people on the way out. And people were like, 'those are the hug guys, I didn't get my hug.' And we're like, all right, cool. The hug guys.
The hug brothers. Hug forever. Hug a thug. Yeah, it was pretty awesome. And the Yeah Yeah Yeahs were awesome, you guys were awesome. Did you get to hug any goths? Did you find any goths to hug?
We did. They're so emotional, you know? There's a lot of-- I don't know. The Yeah Yeah Yeahs attract a lot of different kinds of-- I don't know. For me, as a Korean, Karen O is my...

...I think she's married now, right? But a few years ago she was my celeb crush. I was like, oh fuck, she'd probably be so awesome to be my girlfriend, hang out and have fun. Your non-relationship. My fantasy relationship. That's the other thing -- you want to talk about fantasy on the...
...road -- it's to fantasize about a rock star or a celebrity. I'm at the point now where I've met some of my heroes, and I'm like, you know, wish that never happened.

Yeah, it's better -- your mind is amazing, you know? It builds up these fantastical scenarios, and then once you meet them you're like, oh. Yeah. It's better just to imagine what things would have been like.
I feel like it's usually kind of a disappointment. Yeah. I mean, I haven't met that many, but the few I've met, yeah. Who did you want to meet? I don't want to say. Why? Okay--

...like, there's this one comedian that I think is so fucking funny. All right, who is it? I don't want to say, I really don't want to say. Usually I'll say anything, but I don't want to say. Is he relevant? He's relevant now, he's hot now -- not aesthetically hot. All right, all right, so -- no...
No, no, no, he's younger. But anyway, he doesn't give off a sleazy vibe or anything. Okay. But anyway, I found out he was a fan, and I'm a fan, so we started talking.

All right. But he would always hit me up at like four in the morning with these really desperate coke calls -- 'come over.' Like only the kind of desperate you can be on coke, or on drugs, at four in the morning.

And it just -- I don't know, it really tainted my image of him. I don't do coke, but I send out some pretty desperate shit. That's true. But your desperate is charming. Oh, thank you. It's different. I think for me it's 50-50, but I kind of don't want to meet people anymore. You guys have met everybody--
...between you guys, you've met everybody. So what do you say about all that shit?
I mean, I met everybody through Mark. And are you, like, glad you met that person, or are you like, fuck, shit? I don't know. I think I have a pretty good filter.

Like, I totally love their films, music, whatever, but I don't think I'd want to hang out with them. Right, that's how I feel about most people I'm a fan of. I appreciate them for what they do, and then that's it.

Right. But I hung out with Bernie Worrell -- he's a cool motherfucker -- like two days ago. We recorded and shit. That's awesome. And he's cool? Fuck yeah, he's super cool. I feel like with musicians it'd be different. Musicians are a little different, they're just cool in general. A lot of times I find...

...the more amazing they are, the more tweaked they are, too. The less talented people can a lot of times be the coolest, nicest ones. And then the princes of the world, the geniuses -- they're so weird and fucked up. And that's why they can make that weird world.

Yeah, that's why -- because they have a totally different perspective on the world than everybody else. Like, I feel like all the black dudes who idolize Scarface and have Al Pacino posters, Scarface tattoos--

They're like, oh man -- like every rapper in the '90s. Yeah, they're like, 'if I ever met Al Pacino, it'd be like hanging out with Scarface.' And it's like, no -- you'd be hanging out with a theater nerd.

First of all, Al Pacino is the most overrated actor ever. Right? [mock voice] Hoo-ah! Yeah, that's what I'm saying. I mean, I like Al Pacino, but you wouldn't be hanging out with Scarface. Well, yeah.
You wouldn't be hanging out with-- he'd be like, [mock voice] 'oh, when I did Scent of a Woman.' Yeah.

So what's the plan right now for you guys? Are you based here? I'm in Los Angeles. We're all based in Los Angeles, except for Derrick -- he bounces between Prague, where his child and his baby's mama are, and Sao Paulo.
Derrick couldn't be here because he's doing the Sepultura album right now, right? Yeah, he was doing it, they finished, and he went back to Sao Paulo today. That shit sounds sick, by the way.
I got to record on it the other day. Really? Yeah. Ross Robinson. Oh, shit. Ross Robinson is producing it. Wait, you're going to be on it? I just recorded it. I heard it, man.

I was over there the other night, it sounds dope, man. It sounds great. It sounds like you did some incredible bongo-band shit on it. Yeah. It's dope. For those of you who don't know, Ross Robinson -- legendary producer of all the Korn albums, and then he revitalized the sound of Vanilla Ice.
He did Vanilla Ice -- he re-recorded 'Ice Ice Baby' in the style of Korn. It's pretty sick.

Deftones. Deftones. He's the new-metal dude. And then -- let's get deep with the supergroup. Any band -- you guys will probably be better at this than me -- but first, who are all the supergroups? There was Audioslave, there was Velvet Revolver...

Temple of the Dog. Temple of the Dog. Who was the early one, a long time ago, with Jefferson Starship? Cream. The Yardbirds. Traveling Wilburys. Oh yeah. And the Yardbirds -- that was their supergroup before they were rock stars, all those guys, right? So throughout history there have been supergroups...

...and they don't last. So what's the goal of Maximum Hedrum? Do you want to take it as far as it goes, or is it 'let's see what happens,' or is there a specific plan? Maximum Hedrum is all about just having fun. That's really the main thing -- just have fun.

When we made the record it was all about that -- that was the only rule. Like, hey, are we having fun right now? No? Okay, let's do something else. Same thing with touring. And I'm sure we'll do more music, just because we all have so much...

...fucking fun together. The tour was just constantly cracking up, doing dumb shit and having a blast, and I'm sure that'll carry into the next record. Even when the band breaks down. How long have you guys been a band?

I mean, we-- that was our first tour ever. Five minutes? That was our first tour. So is there band drama yet? No band drama. No band drama. That's good, nobody's pissed off yet. But here's the thing -- the whole supergroup thing is the commitment. Derrick's doing his thing, you're doing yours, everyone's...

...doing a million projects. So it's that whole scatterbrain thing of, what takes priority, how much are we all going to commit? I'm basically asking you these questions because I'm trying to figure that shit out with this. We're sort of a supergroup, trying to figure out our legs and how this is all going to work. I think when we're...

...together, we give it our all, regardless of it being a supergroup. I came in after the fact -- they'd already made the record. Oh, really? I recorded maybe some Latin percussion on one song. And then when they started thinking about the band, they're like, who are we going to get? Fuck it, let's ask Fredo. What are you doing? I was...

...like, yeah, what's up, let's play some music. It's what I do best. And now it's like, okay, now we've got to go on the road, now we've got to perform it -- what the fuck, right? Are you available? Are you available? It's weird to get the call...

...and go, 'are you available?' and be like, yeah, fuck yeah. It was awesome. You guys are a fun band to watch. Well, thanks, man. I missed those shows -- they did a residency at Los Globos here in Los Angeles, every Monday, with...
If the band doesn't work out, you guys are always open to join our supergroup. We have one -- Money Mark, right here. Do you guys have any supergroup drama yet?

All we are is drama. Someone's already been fired. Yeah, we had a guy fired -- well, he quit. Fired, quit, came back, and then fired, quit again, or whatever, I don't know. It happens. We've got to start some shit because we need some press. Yeah, we were thinking, hey, maybe you guys can help us figure this out. We were thinking, just...

...because this is a brand-new project nobody knows about, we were trying to think of some crazy publicity shit, a totally retarded publicity stunt. One thing we were thinking about was doing a fake sex tape with Derrick and, like...
...somebody who looks like a Kardashian, and then somehow-- But why does it have to be fake? Can it just be real? He's got a baby. And a baby mama. Is he in a relationship with her?
